My goal is to maximize my value. The key insight is that my ranking only matters within the "obtainable set" of schools that would accept me. I need to figure out which schools are potentially obtainable and then rank them according to my preferences.

School w: I have priority 1. This means I'm very likely to be accepted if I apply. So, w is highly likely to be in my obtainable set.

School x: I have priority 2. Since most applicants favor y > x > w > z, there's a good chance x will be competitive. However, priority 2 is still decent. x *might* be in my obtainable set.

School y: I have priority 1. This means I'm very likely to be accepted if I apply. So, y is highly likely to be in my obtainable set.

School z: I have priority 2. Since most applicants favor y > x > w > z, z is probably the least competitive. Priority 2 is decent. z *might* be in my obtainable set.

My values are: z = $68 > x = $67 > y = $62 > w = $48.

Since w and y are almost certainly obtainable, I need to rank them relative to x and z.

If both x and z are obtainable, I want z > x > y > w.
If only x is obtainable, I want x > y > w > z.
If only z is obtainable, I want z > y > w > x.
If neither x nor z are obtainable, I want y > w > x > z.

Since z has the highest value, I want to rank it first. x is the next highest value, so it should be ranked second. Then y and then w.

Ranking z first ensures that if z is obtainable, I will get it. Ranking x second ensures that if z is not obtainable but x is, I will get x. Ranking y third ensures that if neither z nor x are obtainable, I will get y. Ranking w last ensures that I only get w if nothing else is available.
